title: Register of Usage Limits per Program, Hardship Assistance Programs
content:
How often each of the Hardship Assistance Programs may be used on one loan, the spacing between plans of the same program, the wait after a broken plan and whether the plan's months count toward the rolling 24-month relief limit are registered here per program.

| Program | Counts toward the 24-month relief limit | Most plans per loan over its life | Whole calendar months between plans of the same program | Calendar days after a broken plan before a new request |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Short-Term Payment Deferral | yes | 2 | 6 | 90 |
| Reduced Payment Plan | yes | 2 | 6 | 90 |
| Temporary Rate Reduction Plan | yes | 1 | 12 | 90 |
| Term Extension Modification | yes | 1 | 0 | 180 |
| Disaster Relief Deferral | no | no limit | 0 | 0 |
| Servicemember Rate Cap Benefit | no | no limit | 0 | 0 |
| Charged-Off Settlement Plan | no | 1 | 0 | 90 |

## Meaning of each column

- **Counts toward the relief limit**: whether the plan's months count toward the rolling 24-month relief limit.
- **Most plans per loan**: most plans of this program per loan over its life; "no limit" when unlimited.
- **Months between plans**: whole calendar months that must pass after a plan of the same program ends before another can start on the loan; 0 when none.
- **Wait after a broken plan**: calendar days after a broken plan before any new request on the loan is taken (other than Disaster Relief or Servicemember benefits).

## Hypothetical reading

A loan that has already had one Temporary Rate Reduction Plan has used that program's single permitted plan; the same loan with one earlier Reduced Payment Plan may still have a second one, once 6 whole calendar months have passed since the first ended.
